issues: Key rests on the documented limit (website endpoint: no HTTPS to the origin; S3 REST origin: HTTPS follows the viewer protocol policy). Minor: switching to the standard S3 origin drops website-endpoint behavior (index document per folder, redirects); the stem does not say the site needs it, so the key stands, but a reviewer could argue the change is not 'least overhead' for a site that depends on it.

Key documented (Legacy Clients Support for non-SNI clients, additional monthly charges). No price in the item. The doc adds that Legacy Clients Support limits the available security policies and recommends SNI when viewers support it; not a problem for the key because the stem says the clients do not support SNI.

Conceptual overlap with certificate-office-009 (imported certificate is not eligible for managed renewal; request a DNS-validated ACM certificate). Different services (CloudFront vs ALB) and 010 adds the us-east-1 rule, so acceptable; 017 repeats the imported-certificate distractor.

Wrong option 'Switch the validation ... from DNS to email': the why says validation 'cannot be switched between DNS and email', but the cited quote (acm-email-validation) documents only the opposite direction ('After you create a certificate with email validation, you cannot switch to validating it with DNS'). The DNS-to-email direction is not in the evidence or in the ACM pages checked, so the why asserts an undocumented fact.

Wrong option 'Delete the certificate from the distribution and associate it again to restart the renewal': the why says removal 'stops automatic renewal rather than restarting it'. The documented reason it fails is that the missing CNAME record is what blocks validation (renewal status page: check that the DNS record exists and the certificate remains in use); re-associating would not restore the record. The why is an oversimplification and re-association could make the certificate 'in use' again.
suggestedFix: Reword the DNS-to-email option's why to the documented point ('email validation would need someone to act on emails and does not restore the missing DNS record; ACM renews a DNS-validated certificate automatically when the CNAME is in place') or change the option to the documented direction. Reword the re-associate option's why: 'The certificate stays Pending validation until the CNAME record exists again; removing and re-adding it does not recreate the record.'

issues: Judged as asked: yes, documented. acm-bestpractices.html: 'To renew a certificate, ACM generates a new public-private key pair. If your application pins the ACM certificate and the certificate is successfully renewed with a new public key, the application might be unable to connect to your domain.' and 'If you're using a public certificate, pin your application to all available Amazon root certificates.' No ACM page checked (managed renewal, public certificates, exportable certificates, ACME) documents a setting to reuse the same public key on renewal, and a web search of AWS docs found none. So the wrong option 'Ask ACM to reuse the same public key' fails on a documented fact (new key pair on renewal); the absence of a reuse setting is inferred from the documented behavior, which is acceptable. A second documented route (import your own certificate and pin to it) is in the same doc but not offered, and it would not be 'least ongoing effort' anyway.
Minor: the wrong option 'Pin the app to the ARN' is near-absurd (an ARN is not in the TLS handshake).
suggestedFix: Optional: in the 'reuse the same public key' why, add 'AWS documents that renewal generates a new key pair and describes no setting to keep the old key.'
